title: Crypto recovery stalls, tokenized collateral expands, portfolio falls 3.3%
paragraphs: Bitcoin slipped about 1% over 24 hours to around $60,000, while ether fell 1.2% to roughly $1,700. Total crypto market capitalization edged down 0.1% to $2.15 trillion. Trading was mixed beneath those headline numbers: several major altcoins gained, while BNB weakened. The Economic Times reports continued ETF outflows and subdued institutional demand as headwinds to the recovery. Bitcoin and ether remain down roughly 7% over the week, so the latest stabilization has recovered only part of the sell-off.

The European Central Bank has approved a wider route for tokenized securities to qualify as collateral for its lending operations. Securities issued on platforms licensed under the EU distributed ledger pilot regime will be eligible subject to existing collateral standards and additional operational requirements. Implementation is planned for June 2027. Banks will still need access through approved securities depositories and settlement infrastructure. This could make qualifying tokenized bonds more useful for funding, although the necessary platform requirements are still being finalized.

The US Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture claim covering more than $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the Binance theft. The department attributes the attack to North Korean actors and says US authorities have helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion across the broader recovery effort. The new action concerns assets already restrained. It advances the legal recovery process, but the filing alone does not establish that the money has been returned to customers.

The European Commission also proposed new sanctions targeting Russian banks and crypto platforms, including a dedicated crypto sanctions task force. All 27 EU members must approve the package before it takes effect, and negotiations may change the measures. For platforms serving cross-border customers, the proposal signals possible additional restrictions on counterparties and payment routes. Its immediate significance is the direction of enforcement policy; the announced package is still a proposal.

Our on-chain portfolio is worth about $52,514: $8,690 in the active treasury and $43,824 in the Safe. Its marked value fell $1,780, or 3.3%, from the previous comparable snapshot. Direct ARC holdings account for about $36,231, or 69% of the total, before the Safe's $5,192 WETH/ARC pool adds further exposure. Beefy pools total $1,697. The Safe's direct ARC balance is unchanged, while its value fell about $1,425, accounting for most of the portfolio decline.

Aave holds about $5,810 of WETH collateral against $3,154 of USDC debt. Treasury and Safe health factors eased to 1.77 and 1.41, from 1.79 and 1.43. Fluid has about $155 in net value against $1,067 of debt, with its health factor still at 1.03. That remains the narrowest lending safety margin in the portfolio.

sources.title: Bitcoin hovers near $60,000, Ethereum at $1,700 as crypto market attempts recovery after sell-off; institutional flows, US data in focus
